summary: Implemented checklist-aware core normalization and validation for the Phase 1 container layer, including primitive-shape sanity checks, simulation-bound validation, explicit unsupported-feature errors, normalize-index handling, zero-dimension boundary coercion, and supporting tests/docs.
key_findings: Added `autofdtd.core.validation` as the shared normalization layer for tagged component payloads, covering name trimming, vector coercion, primitive geometry checks for `Box`/`Sphere`/`Cylinder`, structure-bound checks against the simulation domain, and zero-size-axis boundary coercion to `Periodic`.

`Simulation` now exposes explicit Phase 1 control-policy fields for `normalize_index`, `relax_courant`, `low_freq_smoothing`, and `lumped_elements`, with implemented validation for normalize-index and clear fail-fast errors for deferred or rejected core features.

Unsupported feature handling is now tied directly to the local feature matrix through lookup helpers in `autofdtd.planning`, so deferred and reject-clearly feature tags fail with explicit messages instead of being accepted silently or rejected as unknown extras.

Coverage now includes normalization, primitive shape errors, out-of-domain warnings and errors, zero-dimension absorbing-boundary coercion, normalize-index validation, and planning lookups, with docs and working memory updated to point later tasks at the shared validator path.

Validation coverage for normalization, shape constraints, unsupported features, domain bounds, and zero-dimension boundary coercion.
Architecture notes describing the new shared validation layer and its current responsibilities.
Distilled task handoff notes for later feature-family tasks to reuse the core validation path.
Structured task result artifact for this loop iteration.

follow_up_notes: Verification passed with `ruff check`, `pytest -q`, and `mypy src`. Geometry, material, boundary, source, monitor, and grid tasks should extend `autofdtd.core.validation` rather than duplicating checklist-driven policy checks in each family.
